questions: Must resolving an attempt record when it was resolved, or must the lifecycle rule be changed because ResolveAttemptChange supplies no resolution time?

quotes: Records of the kinds that are never edited — issued contract versions, implementations, trial cases, flow versions, values, verdicts, activations and trace records — are only ever written once; for any other entity a lifecycle change — a status, who decided, resolved, revoked, cancelled or released and when, concluded_at, ended_at, waiting points, outputs, a run's resumptions — updates those fields of the entity's one record in place, and the record keeps its store position, the position of its creation; no other field of a written record ever changes.
ResolveAttemptChange fields (exact, no others exist): change: Literal['resolve_attempt'], attempt: AttemptKey, resolution: AttemptResolution

EffectAttempt fields (exact, no others exist): run_id: str, node_id: str, map_index: int | None, attempt_number: int, binding_id: str, inputs: tuple[PortRef, ...], idempotency_key: str | None, authority: Authority, status: AttemptStatus, recorded_at: KernelInstant, concluded_at: KernelInstant | None, resolved_by: Actor | None
judgement.why: The lifecycle rule requires recording when an attempt was resolved, but neither ResolveAttemptChange nor EffectAttempt has a resolution-time field.

topics.topic: Whether existing StoredValue records must be rewritten
questions: Must every StoredValue listed by a change be written, or is an already-existing StoredValue explicitly exempt from the all-listed-records-must-be-written rule?

judgement.why: P2 already judged the same unchanged question and established that an existing StoredValue is returned without being rewritten.

precedent.topic: RecordSet inclusion or return of an existing unchanged StoredValue
quotes: A StoredValue whose value_id already exists is not written again and the existing record is returned in its place, since equal values share one identity; spooled files must already be published in the run's spool by spool_file before the change that writes their SpooledFile records.

Any other broken invariant (a linked record missing, an identity already present for an immutable record, a status change from a status the change does not start from) or a failed transaction raises StoreInternalError with nothing written.
precedent.why: The specific StoredValue rule requires returning the existing record without rewriting it, while the phrase “Any other broken invariant” excludes that stated special case.

topics.topic: Whether open_store removes orphaned published spool files
questions: Must the next open remove unnamed published spool files left by failed changes, or must open_store never remove spool files?

quotes: Durability order: every file a change names is published, fsynced and its directory fsynced before the change is committed, and the SQLite database runs with synchronous FULL, so after a power loss a committed record never names a missing or partial file; a file published by a change that then failed stays unnamed until the next start removes it (A18 rule 4).

Returns StoreOpened with data_directory and temporary_files_removed, the count of temporary files removed, unnamed value files not counted; no record, named value file or spool is removed by this call.
judgement.why: One passage requires the next start to remove every unnamed file published by a failed change, while the open_store return rule says that this call removes no spool.

questions: Must the module alone assign attempt_number inside the transaction, or must the caller supply it in SpooledFileKey before the transaction while spool_file does not assign it?

quotes: The module alone assigns, inside the transaction: store positions; the random identities trial_execution_id, binding_id, run_id, approval_id and grant_id, drawn from a cryptographically secure source and drawn again on a collision, which is a drawn identity for which the row's load operation finds a row; attempt_number; and every by-field (issued_by, created_by, submitted_by, added_by, activated_by, executed_by, proposed_by, accepted_by, authored_by, started_by, cancelled_by, resumed_by, released_by, decided_by, granted_by, revoked_by, resolved_by) from the actor argument; and each status the field-assignment note of a variant says it writes or sets (proposed, accepted, requested, approved, refused, active, revoked, in_flight and the rest); every other field, times included, comes from the change as given.
The attempt_number of the key is the element's next number as the caller read it; spool_file does not assign one.
judgement.why: The first passage reserves attempt_number assignment to the module inside the transaction, while the second requires the caller to put that number in the key before spool_file and says spool_file does not assign it.

topics.topic: Required handling when a multipart file port has no media_type
questions: Must file-carriage ports be guaranteed to have a non-None media_type, or must prepare_request reject or otherwise handle a file port whose media_type is None instead of using it as the required Content-Type value?
Must media_type be required for every file port, or must a missing file media_type produce a specified PreSendFailure or receive a specified string fallback?

judgement.why: This asks the same question as P6, and neither the relevant text nor its quoted passages has changed.

precedent.topic: How multipart file parts handle a null media_type
quotes: prepare_request: [BEHAVIOR] For POST, PUT and PATCH without a file input the inputs not used in the path form one JSON object keyed by port name, sent as its RFC 8785 canonical bytes with content type application/json; with a file input the body is multipart/form-data with one part per input not used in the path in port name order, one part per file in list order for a many file port, each part having exactly the two headers Content-Disposition form-data with name set to the port, plus filename set to the port for a file part, and Content-Type, the port's media type for a file part and application/json without parameters for a value part whose content is the canonical JSON bytes.

prepare_request: [VALIDATION_ERROR] An input is not placeable, giving input_not_placeable with the port named, when a placeholder value is not a non-null string or integer, or a GET or DELETE query value is not a string, integer, number, boolean, null or list of those; inputs are examined in port name order and a list's elements in list order, and the first that cannot be placed is named; an input placed in the path is placed nowhere else.

Port fields (exact, no others exist): name: str, direction: PortDirection, value_schema: str, carriage: Carriage, media_type: str | None, cardinality: Cardinality, disclosure_class: DisclosureClass | None
precedent.why: The model permits a missing media type, while multipart file parts require that value and the specified placement failures do not say how this case ends.

topics.topic: Whether cleanup_failed changes include newly determined skipped_by_guard and upstream_failed executions
questions: For cleanup_failed, must the change also contain every newly determined skipped_by_guard and upstream_failed execution, or must it contain only the cleanup_failed execution?

quotes: After each function element MUST write one RecordRunProgressChange through record_change with the given actor, holding that element's execution, its StoredValues and SpooledFiles, and every skipped_by_guard and upstream_failed record that became determined, executions sorted by (node_id, map_index), with status running;

When a function element's outcome is crashed with detail cleanup_failed MUST write that one execution in a RecordRunProgressChange with status running and the waiting points unchanged, execute and reach nothing more, write no other status, and raise StopRequiredError.
judgement.why: The general function-element rule requires newly determined skipped and upstream-failed executions in the change, while the cleanup_failed rule requires that one execution.

topics.topic: Whether ended_at belongs to FunctionElementOutcome or only to NodeExecutionDraft
questions: Must ended_at be added to FunctionElementOutcome, or must the return-shape note state explicitly that ended_at is the NodeExecutionDraft's ended_at rather than a FunctionElementOutcome field?

quotes: Returns FunctionElementOutcome with the NodeExecutionDraft, ended_at taken when the outcome is built, and the StoredValues and SpooledFiles of its outputs, each of the class highest_disclosure_class gives for the classes of every input value and file the element received — an input file list counting with its SpooledFilesRef's disclosure_class, even when empty — and each output SpooledFilesRef with that same class, so no output is of a lower class than an input.
FunctionElementOutcome fields (exact, no others exist): execution: NodeExecutionDraft, stored_values: tuple[StoredValue, ...], spooled_files: tuple[SpooledFile, ...]
judgement.why: The return-shape note grammatically assigns ended_at to FunctionElementOutcome, whose exact model fields contain no ended_at field.

topics.topic: Whether mapped operation elements with waiting concluded records are revisited or excluded on first passage
questions: Must a mapped operation element whose concluded record waits be executed/reached again, or must the first passage exclude waiting elements?

quotes: A mapped node, once selected, takes its elements in list order, executing every element with no concluded record that does not wait, before the next node is selected;
operation elements that wait are not reached again here.
judgement.why: The mapped-node rule includes elements whose concluded record waits, while the operation rule forbids reaching waiting operation elements again during advance_run.

topics.topic: Precedence of Origin validation versus path and HTTP method routing errors
questions: For a non-POST request to MCP_ENDPOINT_PATH that carries an Origin header, which status must be returned: 405 or 403?
For a request to a path other than MCP_ENDPOINT_PATH that carries an Origin header, which status must be returned: 404 or 403?

judgement.why: P12 answers the method-versus-Origin case, and P14 answers the path-versus-Origin case on the same unchanged passage.

precedent.topic: Whether method rejection or Origin rejection takes precedence for a non-POST MCP-path request
quotes: Only a POST to the path equal to the imported MCP_ENDPOINT_PATH constant reaches answer_request; any other method on that path is answered 405, any other path 404, and a request carrying an Origin header 403, each without a body and without calling answer_request;
precedent.why: The Origin condition is unconditional, while 405 is limited to the correct path and every other path receives 404.

topics.topic: Response body for oversized or unauthorized JSON-RPC notifications and responses
questions: Must an oversized or unauthorized notification/response return empty bytes, or must it return the specified JSON-RPC error response?

judgement.why: P13 answers the same question on the same unchanged passages.

precedent.topic: Whether oversized or unauthenticated notifications and responses return a refusal or empty bytes
quotes: MUST check one request in exactly this order, the first failure deciding: the byte length of request_bytes is within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SURFACE_REQUEST_BYTES_MAX constant, else invalid_request; authenticate_token with presented_token gives an Actor, else unauthorized with one fixed reason that reveals nothing about any record;
The body is one JSON-RPC 2.0 message, read only after the size and token checks.

A JSON object whose jsonrpc is "2.0" with a string method and an id is a request; one with a method and no id is a notification and one with no method a response: both are answered with empty bytes and change nothing.
precedent.why: Size and token checks occur before the body is read and classified, so an oversized or unauthenticated notification or response is refused before the empty-response rule can apply.
